question: Why does G stand seventh in the Latin alphabet, when its Greek ancestor gamma stood third?
answer: Because C already held third place. Etruscan had no g sound, so gamma reached Rome as C, writing k. In the 3rd century BC Rome added a stroke to C to make G and slotted it into seventh place, left empty when Z was dropped. Z came back later, tacked on at the very end.
move: An odd position in a list often marks where something was taken out.
reference: Gordon, Illustrated Introduction to Latin Epigraphy, University of California Press, 1983
